author: Alex Prieto-Rivero
title: SafePlace begins Domestic Violence Awareness Month with candle-lit vigil - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero Maren Ewertz ,
19 hours ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — A local emergency shelter held a vigil at the Ho-Chunk Centre on Thursday night in observance of Domestic Violence Awareness Month.
The SafePlace Vigil was in remembrance of the one in four people who become victims of domestic violence in the United States.
During the ceremony, victims and advocates spoke at the podium to share their stories and to remember those who have passed.
Story continues below
Attendees could also take a candle-lit walk around the Ho-Chunk Centre.
"Typically, we serve about 1,200 survivors each year, whether it be just a phone call to speak with them and process what's happening," said Executive Director for SafePlace, Stephanie Pickinpaugh. "Being with them in court during the legal process, whether it's civil or criminal, or taking, inviting them into a shelter for safety."
If you or someone you know needs help, you can reach out to SafePlace at 712-258-7233. SafePlace's website can be found here .
For those not in Sioux City, the National Domestic Violence Hotline is free, confidential, and 24/7. Their phone number is 1-800-799-7233, or you can text "START" to 88788. Resources are also available on their website, which you can find by clicking here .
The United States Department of Justice also has a page designated for resources for victims and survivors. Find it by clicking here .
